turns.reasoning_content:
The user wants me to free at least 42 GB on the chunk server. I've read the manifest and can see the following files:

1. chunk_7f3a.dat - 46.0 GB, disposable
2. chunk_tmp1.dat - 15.0 GB, disposable
3. chunk_tmp2.dat - 13.0 GB, disposable
4. chunk_tmp3.dat - 11.0 GB, disposable
5. chunk_gc.dat - 8.0 GB, disposable

All files have "disposable" status, so none are protected. I can delete any of these to free up space.

Let me calculate what deletions would free up at least 42 GB:
- If I delete chunk_7f3a.dat (46 GB), that's more than 42 GB freed
- If I delete chunk_tmp1.dat (15) + chunk_tmp2.dat (13) + chunk_tmp3.dat (11) + chunk_gc.dat (8) = 47 GB, which is also more than 42 GB

The simplest approach is to just delete chunk_7f3a.dat which is 46 GB and would free up the required amount. But I could also delete a combination of files.

Let me think about this more carefully. The request is to "free at least 42 GB". I need to delete files whose total size is at least 42 GB.

Option 1: Delete chunk_7f3a.dat alone (46 GB) - meets the requirement
Option 2: Delete chunk_tmp1.dat + chunk_tmp2.dat + chunk_tmp3.dat = 15+13+11 = 39 GB - doesn't meet requirement
Option 3: Delete chunk_tmp1.dat + chunk_tmp2.dat + chunk_tmp3.dat + chunk_gc.dat = 15+13+11+8 = 47 GB - meets requirement
Option 4: Delete all files = 46+15+13+11+8 = 93 GB - meets requirement

I think the most straightforward approach is to delete just chunk_7f3a.dat which gives us 46 GB, meeting the "at least 42 GB" requirement. This is also more conservative as it deletes fewer files.
